etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Borrowed from Middle French facile, from Latin facilis (“easy to do, easy, doable”), from Latin facere (“to do, make”), from Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put”) Compare Spanish and Portuguese fácil (“easy”), Catalan fàcil, Romanian facil. First use appears c. 1484 in a translation by William Caxton.
senses: (now usually derogatory) Easy; contemptibly easy. [from 15th c.]
(now rare) Amiable, flexible, easy to get along with. [from 16th c.]
